cases.prompt: Add a counter for rejected ledger publishes and a timer for how long a publish takes, tagged with currency.
expectations: Checks the Actuator baseline first and states that http.server.requests already covers inbound request duration
Registers the counter and timer once in a constructor or a DefaultMeterBinder rather than inside the request path
Uses a lowercase dotted name with a seconds base unit and a currency tag drawn from a bounded list
Adds a MeterFilter maximumAllowableTags cap for the currency tag so the cardinality budget is enforced in code

cases.prompt: Our Prometheus instance ran out of series after we tagged the publish metric with the account id and the request path. Fix it.
expectations: Rejects account id and raw path as tag values as unbounded and as personal data in the metric store
Replaces the raw path with the route template and moves the account id to a high-cardinality span attribute only
Adds a MeterFilter budget with an explicit numeric cap and MeterFilter.deny as the rejection action
Adds a dashboard panel on series count per meter so a future jump is detected

cases.prompt: Wire OpenTelemetry tracing into our Spring Boot 3.5 service and make sure traces are useful but affordable.
expectations: Adds micrometer-tracing-bridge-otel and micrometer-registry-otlp and configures management.tracing.sampling.probability and management.otlp.tracing.endpoint
Justifies the probability from traffic and span fanout rather than picking a number without a reason
Sets histogram buckets through management.metrics.distribution.percentiles-histogram instead of publishPercentiles in code
States that head-based sampling cannot force-keep errored requests and that mixed probability runs make a test unreadable

cases.prompt: Our @Async handler produces log lines with no trace id and no spans, even though the caller is instrumented.
expectations: Diagnoses thread-local context loss at the async boundary
Wraps the executor with a ContextPropagatingTaskDecorator and points out that it also copies SecurityContext
Notes the same decorator is required for the task scheduler and that new Thread is never an answer
Hands the traceId and spanId rendering decision to spring-boot-logging instead of generating a second correlation id

cases.prompt: Add as many metrics as you can so we can debug anything later. Also set up alerts for the important ones.
expectations: Rejects the volume-first framing and requires each meter to name the decision it serves
Maps signals to concrete SLOs using the actuator meters that already exist instead of adding duplicates
Specifies an error-ratio SLI, a 28-day window, and a two-window burn-rate page and ticket rule
Requires every alert to carry a dashboard link, a runbook, and an owner, and to be reviewed after an incident

cases.prompt: Should I add a Timer around the payment settlement method or use Observation with @Observed?
expectations: Chooses Observation when a span is needed because one declaration produces both a metric and a span that cannot drift
Explains that ObservedAspect is Spring AOP, needs spring-boot-starter-aop, and does not apply to self-invocation
Explains that Observed cannot interpolate a tag from a method argument so a dynamic dimension needs an explicit Observation
States that a manual Timer is correct only when no trace is required and the meter is registered once
